perf.summary: Same even-skip / wheel opportunity as DivisorCount: test 2 then odd p only.
perf.currentCost: `for (long p = 2; p*p <= n; p++)` walks every integer to sqrt(n). Even candidates >=4 contribute a wasted p*p multiply and a `n % p` idiv (the dominant cost) that never succeeds after the factor 2 is stripped.
perf.proposedChange: Handle p=2 separately (compute its geometric-sum factor with a dedicated loop), then iterate `for (long p = 3; p*p <= n; p += 2)`. Optionally a 2-3-5 wheel for further candidate reduction.
perf.rationale: Halves (or more) the number of expensive 64-bit modulo and multiply operations on the trial-division hot path. Same big-O, ~2x smaller constant.
perf.risk: Same `p*p` overflow caveat as the original near long.MAX; stride change does not alter it. Geometric-sum accumulator `sum` and `result` overflow for large highly-composite n exactly as today — behavior preserved.
